module: Define the release and assessment boundary

lesson.title: Follow the product-law route
lesson.summary: Find the sector procedure and its additional AI evidence.

prerequisites.reason: Sector assessment can only be selected after distinguishing the Annex I route and its scope limits.

blocks: A **sector assessment** is the conformity procedure under a particular Union product law. For high-risk systems covered by Annex I Section A, Article 43(3) directs the provider to the relevant sector procedure. The AI Act Section 2 requirements form part of that assessment; Article 17 quality management and specified Annex VII points also apply.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 43(3); Annex I Section A

blocks: The specified Annex VII elements are point 3, points 4.3–4.5, the fifth paragraph of 4.6 and point 5. They concern quality management, technical evidence/assessment, changes and surveillance. Their inclusion does not mean you mechanically run two entirely separate assessment procedures.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 43(3); Annex I Section A

blocks: Where sector law offers an assessment without a third party conditioned on harmonised standards, the provider must also meet Article 43(3)'s complete AI requirement-coverage condition through standards or, where applicable, common specifications. High-risk classification alone does not force a third party where sector law does not require that choice. This is a conditional option, not permission to ignore Article 6(1)'s classification test.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 43(3); Annex I Section A

blocks: **Dual-route priority:** where the same system falls under both Annex I Section A and Annex III, the relevant sector procedure applies. Harbour's case stipulates the sector-required third party. Adding an Annex III use does not automatically change it to the employment internal-control route.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 43(3); Annex I Section A

blocks: A sector-notified body needs the specified Article 31(4), (5), (10) and (11) competence/independence assessment evidence for transitional AI assessment powers, and must apply for Section 4 designation by 28 January 2028. Verify that evidence; a sector badge alone is insufficient. Real device class and current sector procedure remain separate source lookups.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 43(3); Annex I Section A

questions.prompt: Harbour follows its required medical-product procedure. Where do AI Section 2 requirements belong?

options.blocks: Within the relevant sector conformity assessment.
options.reason: Article 43(3) incorporates them and the specified additional elements.

options.blocks: Outside the assessment because sector law replaces them.
options.reason: They remain part of the assessment.
Descriptions do not substitute for assessment evidence.

questions.prompt: The same Harbour system also has an Annex III use. Which assessment procedure controls?

options.blocks: The Annex III route automatically replaces sector procedure.
options.reason: The amended paragraph gives the sector procedure priority.

options.blocks: The provider may choose whichever route has less paperwork.
options.reason: Convenience is not the legal route-selection rule.
Article 43(3)'s final subparagraph establishes this priority.

options.blocks: Assume no sector body can ever assess AI requirements.
options.reason: The paragraph provides conditional transitional powers.

options.blocks: Verify the required assessment evidence and designation timetable.
options.reason: The transitional powers are conditional on specified checks.

options.blocks: Accept the offer solely because it has a sector badge.
options.reason: The badge alone does not demonstrate the additional conditions.
